400	In any case, what I'm trying to say is that Abraham and Isaac were, Sarah and Abraham were
401	tumtumim.	"tumtum" (sexually undifferentiated).
402	And Yitzchak and Rivka were barren, and Yaakov and Rachel were barren, and Leah too was barren,
403	as it says, "HaShem saw that Leah was hated and opened her womb" — meaning she was closed until He opened her. All of them
404	barren.
405	The Gemara asks: why?
406	Why?
407	It answers:
408	because the Holy One, blessed be He, desires the prayers of the righteous.
409	So I understand that Yitzchak prayed for himself. What is this: "And Yitzchak entreated HaShem opposite
410	his wife Rivka, because she was barren."
411	Why, you were barren too! So what is "she was barren"?
412	Meaning, she was barren — you weren't barren.
413	A big question.
414	So in years past I wrote a few answers to this, a few answers on this, and it was already printed in my book Merkavot
415	Argaman LaTorah.
416	Today I want to briefly go over the answers I brought, and add one more answer that only came to me today.
417	Of course it's not in the book, because it only came to me today.
418	Maybe one day when I publish the...
419	with the help of HaShem, when I publish my novellae on the Torah in five volumes, may the words of Torah increase and multiply,
420	the Torah, words of Torah be fruitful and multiply, then maybe we'll put this novel idea in there too.
421	But after all, why does it say "because she was barren"?
422	So I said, there's Bava Kama, page 92b, where the Gemara says, whoever prays for his fellow while needing the same thing himself,
423	is answered first.
424	If you need something and you pray for yourself, the attribute of judgment accuses you: he doesn't deserve it, he spoke lashon
425	hara, he doesn't have enough merits, he has transgressions.
426	But when you pray for your friend, the abundance descends straight to the friend.
427	By the way, what reaches the friend reaches you first, because you are the cause of opening the upper
428	spring, and then it goes to him.
429	And therefore, whoever prays for his fellow while needing the same thing himself is answered first.
430	According to this, it is clear and simple why Yitzchak prays for her.
431	"Because she was barren."
432	Meaning, he prays for her.
433	He too was barren.
434	But he says, it is better to pray for her; if I pray for her, the Holy One, blessed be He, will answer me, and you'll see that it really is
435	so.
436	It is written there, "And HaShem was entreated by him." Why not "by her"?
437	Why not?
438	Because he was the one who prayed.
439	So whoever prays for his fellow while needing the same thing himself is answered first, and so it was; it seems brilliant to me.
